theory.intro: When a point is translated (slid) or reflected (flipped), its coordinates change in a predictable way.
steps: For a translation, add the across and up/down moves.
For a reflection, change the sign of the coordinate that crosses the axis.

foundation.question_text:
Translate $A(-3,2)$ $4$ units right.
Give the image coordinates.

Translate $B(2,-1)$ $5$ units down.
Give the image coordinates.
Translate $C(-4,-2)$ $3$ units right and $5$ units up.

Points $P$ and $P'$ are shown.
Describe the single transformation from $P$ to $P'$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.66]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-5)grid(5,5);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-5.5)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-4,2)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$P$};\fill(3,2)circle(2.5pt)node[above right]{$P'$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
foundation.solution_text:
The $y$-coordinate stays $2$.
The $x$-coordinate changes from $-4$ to $3$, a move of $7$ units right.
Translate $7$ units right.

development.question_text:
Translate $F(5,-3)$ $8$ units left.
Give the image coordinates.

Point $G(-2,-5)$ is translated to $G'(-2,1)$.
Describe the translation.
development.solution_text:
The $x$-coordinate is unchanged.
$1-(-5)=6$
Translate $6$ units up.

development.question_text:
Point $H(4,1)$ is translated $7$ units left and $3$ units down.
Find $H'$.

The point $J$ is shown.
Reflect it in the $x$-axis and write the coordinates of $J'$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.68]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-4,-4)grid(4,4);\draw[<->](-4.5,0)--(4.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-2,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$J$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
Keep $x=-2$ and change the sign of $y$.
$J'=(-2,-3)$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.68]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-4,-4)grid(4,4);\draw[<->](-4.5,0)--(4.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-2,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$J$};\fill(-2,-3)circle(2.5pt)node[below left]{$J'$};\draw[dashed](-2,3)--(-2,-3);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

development.question_text:
The point $K$ is shown.
Reflect it in the $y$-axis and write the coordinates of $K'$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.66]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-4)grid(5,4);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(4,-2)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$K$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
development.solution_text:
Keep $y=-2$ and change the sign of $x$.
$K'=(-4,-2)$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.66]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-4)grid(5,4);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(4,-2)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$K$};\fill(-4,-2)circle(2.5pt)node[below left]{$K'$};\draw[dashed](4,-2)--(-4,-2);\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

development.question_text:
Points $L(-3,-4)$ and $L'(3,-4)$ are a point and its image.
Name the reflecting axis.
development.solution_text:
The $y$-coordinate stays $-4$ and the sign of $x$ changes.
The reflecting axis is the $y$-axis.

mastery.question_text:
After a translation $6$ units right and $4$ units down, a point is at $(2,-1)$.
What were its starting coordinates?
mastery.solution_text:
Reverse the moves: $6$ left and $4$ up.
$(2-6,-1+4)$
$=(-4,3)$

mastery.question_text:
A point is reflected in the $x$-axis but its coordinates do not change.
What must be true about the point?
Give an example.
mastery.solution_text:
Reflection in the $x$-axis changes the sign of $y$.
For the point to stay fixed, $y=0$.
For example, $(5,0)$.

mastery.question_text:
Mia says that reflecting $M(-6,2)$ in the $y$-axis gives $(-6,-2)$.
Identify her error and give the correct image.
mastery.solution_text:
Mia changed the sign of $y$, which is reflection in the $x$-axis.
Reflection in the $y$-axis changes the sign of $x$.
$M'=(6,2)$
